title: Back in shape: two friends meet after the exams

script.text: Tom! I almost didn't recognise you. Have you been working out?
If you'd asked me in September, I'd have said I was hopelessly out of shape. I could barely climb the stairs at school without puffing.
And now? Don't tell me you've joined a gym.

Well, I've got a gym membership, which isn't quite the same thing. My cousin gave it to me for my birthday, probably as a hint. He's been going for about two years, though to hear him talk, you'd think he'd been there forever.
That's quite a present. So have you actually used it?

Not at first. For three weeks it sat in my wallet. Then I thought, well, I'd better hit the gym before it expires. I started with twice a week, but after ten days I was so enthusiastic that I went every single evening.
Uh-oh. I can see where this is going.
You've guessed it. I overdid it, and on the eleventh day I pulled a muscle in my back. Nothing dramatic, but I couldn't even tie my shoelaces for a few days.
Oh no! Did you see a doctor?
No, I just rested. I was back after a week, a lot more careful, and I've learnt to warm up properly, which I'd completely ignored before.
Sensible. I never am. I always rush into things. What's your routine now?
Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays. I'm not a morning person at all, so I go after dinner. When I tried going before school, I lasted three days.
What about you? I thought you were the sporty one.
I used to be, but I've gone downhill since the exams. I signed up for a swimming class, but it's been cancelled twice already, which is typical.
You should come with me, honestly. It's much easier to build up stamina with somebody next to you, and you can't make excuses.
Maybe. But I'm not keen on that whole no pain, no gain thing. People at gyms always seem to push themselves far too hard.
That's what I thought, too, but my trainer says it's nonsense. You should feel tired, not in agony. He's actually told me to slow down a little.
Now that's something I could do. Let me think about it, and I'll text you on Friday.

statements: Tom received his gym membership as a birthday present.
Tom's cousin has been training regularly for more than five years.
Tom started going to the gym as soon as he got his membership.
Tom hurt himself during the second week of his training.
Tom's mother taught him how to warm up before exercise.
Kate thinks that people have to push themselves hard to make progress.
Tom's trainer advised him to take things more slowly.
discuss: Is a gym membership a good present? What would you give a friend who wants to get fit?
Why do so many people start a new sport enthusiastically and then give up?
Would you prefer to train with a personal trainer or on your own? Why?
